params.body:
The voice screen could answer one turn more than once. An answer that called two actions asked the model for two follow-up replies, every agent notice got its own reply, and the model answered by itself whenever the speech detector heard something, noise included. That last one is the likely source of the voice repeating "what do you want to do" at the start of a conversation.

The page now answers through the bridge's turn lock (portal-cli `voice/turn.mjs`, merged in portal-cli #41 and served by the bridge at `/turn.mjs`), so there is one implementation for the bridge's written answers and the spoken ones.

## What changes in `resources/views/mobile/voice.blade.php`

- **One reply per turn.** A turn opens on something said or typed, or on notices; nothing else asks for a reply until its answer is done. A late or repeated `response.done` for a turn that already ended is ignored.
- **Actions:** all calls of one answer run first, then one `response.create` carries all their results. The turn ends on an answer without calls, or one that was cut off (barge-in still works: `interrupt_response` stays on).
- **Notices:** agents that finished or wait are folded into one summary (1.5 s window, what waits for approval first) and said in one reply; if Shane speaks meanwhile, his turn takes them along.
- **Noise:** the session switches to `create_response: false`; a turn opens when the transcription is in and is not noise (no letters, only fillers, a stock subtitle line). Noise is deleted from the conversation and not kept in the transcript.
- **No second answer to a line already seen:** a line said while actions ran is in the follow-up reply's context, so its own turn is closed without asking again.
- The per-notice strings (`:name is done (:title)`, `:name waits for your approval (:title)`) are no longer used here and leave `lang/nl.json`; the summary comes from the bridge.

## Trade-off to try on the phone

Waiting for the transcription before answering costs a short moment after each spoken turn (the streaming transcriber usually finishes right after speech ends). It is the price of not answering noise; if it feels slow, the alternative is to keep auto-replies and only cancel replies to noise.

## Checks

- A simulation of the page script against a fake realtime channel (the script extracted from the Blade file, the real `turn.mjs`): noise gets no reply and is deleted; two tool calls give one follow-up; two notices in one look plus a duplicate final give one summary reply after the window; a line said during actions is answered once; a barge-in gets one new reply. The same simulation on the current page fails five of the seven checks.
- `tests/Feature/MobileTest.php` and `ActivityTest.php` pass; the full suite passes except `BuildStampTest`, which fails the same way on unchanged main in a git worktree (no build stamp there).

The Android app (`VoiceSession.kt`) still requests one reply per notice and per tool call; it can take the same lock in a follow-up.
params.title: Voice screen: one reply per turn, notices in one summary, noise unanswered
